production.note: US model years for the S54-engined car. First: BMW NA's release "2001 BMW M Coupe and M Roadster Make World Debut" (January 5, 2001). Last: Cars.com's 2002 BMW M page is the final model year on which the car is listed (carscom-2002-bmw-m); no opened page states in so many words that 2002 was the last model year. The 1999-2000 S52 car is the separate record bmw-z3-m-coupe-e36-8-1999-2000.

body.note: Two-door hatchback-bodied coupe (KBB: "M Coupe 2D"); the open car is the separate M Roadster.

displacementL.note: "3.2 liter"; no cc figure was on any opened page.

aspiration.note: Inferred: BMW describes a high-revving naturally aspirated six; no turbocharger or supercharger.

transmission.note: "Both models come with a heavy-duty 5-speed manual transmission."

powerHp.note: Quote (BMW NA release): "315 hp at 7400 rpm (vs. 333 at 7900)" - the parenthesis is the European rating of the S54. Databases agree: "315 @ 7400" SAE net (carscom-2001-bmw-m); "315 @ 7400 RPM" (kbb-2001-m-coupe).

weightLb.note: PROVISIONAL source class (two agreeing databases; BMW's release gives no figure, saying only that the cars have a "lower curb weight" than the M3). Quote (Cars.com 2001): "Base Curb Weight" "3,131 lbs". KBB 2001: "3131 lbs." (kbb-2001-m-coupe); Cars.com's 2002 page repeats "3,131 lbs." (carscom-2002-bmw-m). The databases print the same figure as for the 1999-2000 S52 car, which may be a carry-over. 5-speed manual, the only configuration offered.

sources.publisher: BMW of North America (release on The Auto Channel)
sources.title: 2001 BMW M Coupe and M Roadster Make World Debut (January 5, 2001)

provisionalNote: Weight (3,131 lb) is provisional: it rests on spec databases (Cars.com and KBB, agreeing), which print the same figure as for the 1999-2000 S52 car and may carry it over; BMW's release gives no curb weight. A BMW NA spec sheet or brochure, or a major-magazine specification panel for the 2001-2002 M Coupe, would replace it. Power (315 hp) is from BMW NA's own release. The 2002 end year also lacks a page saying it in so many words.
reviewNotes: No opened page states that 2002 was the final US model year (Cars.com's 2002 page is simply the last listing), and the databases' 3,131 lb matches the S52 car's figure and may be carried over.
